identity: A UAE primary-school social-studies (الدراسات الاجتماعية) workbook chapter, text-extracted from a page-layout original. It runs two lessons end to end: الدرس الأول on علم إماراتي الحبيبة / يوم العلم, and الدرس الثاني on الساحل الشرقي في بلادي. The stream is not prose. It interleaves lesson-title blocks, objective lists marked أولا/ثانيا, first-person pupil task directives (أقرأ، أكتب، ألاحظ، ألون، أحوط، أرسم، أستنتج، أوضح شفويا), a scripted family dialogue with speaker labels, glossary definition boxes, national-anthem lines with fill-in blanks, and the running page header الدرس الأول / الدرس الثاني, which repeatedly lands inside a paragraph because on the page it was a separate text box.
law: The sentence unit here is the discourse/layout act, not the clause. One heading, one objective line, one task directive, one declarative statement or definition, one dialogue turn, one running header = one sentence. Three operative sub-rules, each confirmed against this document itself. (1) FURNITURE IS ITS OWN UNIT: الدرس الثاني stands alone between <NL> tokens three times (609-610, 745-746, 790-791), proving it is an independent unit, so every mid-paragraph occurrence forces a boundary both on the token before it and on الأول/الثاني itself. (2) ASYNDETIC DIRECTIVE JUXTAPOSITION BREAKS, و-COORDINATION DOES NOT: two first-person-imperfect task verbs set side by side with no connective are two sentences (أتعرف|أكتب at 176, أرسم|ألاحظ at 222, أكتب|أذكر at 264, أحوط|ألون at 279, definition|أعبر at 569, أختار|أجمع at 810), whereas a directive chained with و stays one sentence — أبحث...وأكتب (513-529), ألاحظ...وأكتب (779-788), أستخدم...وأرسم (444-456), أتأمل...وأقرأ (385-396). (3) THE COLON DOES NOT TERMINATE: حينما قال أتمنى أن نرفع علم الإمارات على كل بيت (39-64) must be one sentence, so a colon never cuts; by the same token the dialogue speaker labels (ماجد، الأب، الأم، راشد، ماجد وراشد) and the glossary head-terms (الموقع الجغرافي، السهل الساحلي، الخور) stay welded to what follows, and the definition boxes read as ordinary nominal sentences (مبتدأ + خبر) in any case.
reasoning: SITE 34 (الإمارات, med). Majid says رأيت اليوم بيوتا كثيرة وقد رفع عليها علم الإمارات and then لماذا يا أبي. The first span is a complete predication, the second an independent vocative question: assertion then interrogation, two illocutionary acts, so I split. The competing reading is a comma before the question, which is common in Arabic school dialogue. This is my least secure split and I flag it for doctrine. || SITES 148, 191, 246+248, 286+288, 322+324, 443, 491, 532, 657 (hi). All are the running header. The decisive one is 148: رئاسة الدولة الدرس الأول cannot be one sentence, yet no punctuation stood between them in the original because the header was a separate text box. That establishes the segmentation here as unit-driven rather than purely punctuation-driven, which licenses every other furniture split. Two of these end on ugly tokens: 246 is الأحمر, sole survivor of a colour list whose other items were image labels, and 322 is يا, the anthem line حصنتك باسم الله يا [وطن] with the blank dropped. The endpoint is forced anyway because the header unambiguously begins at the next token. || SITE 279 (في, med). أحوط على تاريخ إعلان قيام دولتي في ends on a dangling preposition because its object was an image or a blank. ألون at 280 is plainly a new task verb with no و, so the break is real under rule 2; only the ragged endpoint costs confidence. || SITE 233 (الحبيبة, med). عدد ألوان علم إماراتي الحبيبة and شكل علم إماراتي الحبيبة are two parallel fill-in prompts, two table cells sharing an identical tail under different heads عدد and شكل. They are clearly two items, but they are bare noun phrases rather than predications, and NP-fragment splitting is exactly where gold conventions diverge, hence med. || SITE 308 (لدولتي, hi). أستكمل النشيد الوطني لدولتي is a directive to the pupil; عيشي بلادي... is the quoted anthem it introduces. An instruction cannot share a sentence with the material it points at. || SITES 368, 372, 376 (Lesson Two opening). This block mirrors the document opening one for one: [title] / أتعلم عن X / أولا Y / ثانيا Z, which at the start of the document occupied four separate <NL> chunks (0-2, 4-6, 8-11, 13-17) but here collapsed into a single paragraph. So 372 (بلادي before أتعلم) and 376 (الجغرافي before أولا) are hi on that parallel. 368 is only med: الدرس الثاني is a proven standalone unit elsewhere, but on a lesson-opening page it may instead be the colon-joined head of the title (الدرس الثاني: الساحل الشرقي في بلادي), and rule 3 says colons do not cut. The document opening gives no help because it begins at the bare title with no الدرس الأول in front of it. || SITE 810 (يناسبني, hi). أختار ما يناسبني is a choice-box rubric, and at 332-334 it fills an entire <NL> chunk by itself. That self-evidence makes the split before أجمع secure. || DECLINED SPLITS. (a) 312, inside the anthem: عيشي بلادي عاش اتحاد [إماراتنا] and عشت لشعب دينه الإسلام هديه [القرآن] are two verse lines, but they form one continuous quoted citation with no illocutionary break, and verse is not normally cut at line ends. Genuinely uncertain; recorded for doctrine. (b) 89 (نعم): راشد نعم تزامنا مع يوم تولي... — نعم is an answer particle elliptically continuing the mother's turn, comma not stop. (c) Speaker labels and glossary head-terms, per rule 3. (d) All و-coordinated directive pairs, per rule 2. (e) Inside the mother's turn, تسمى ب يوم العلم is a trailing predicate on مناسبة وطنية, not a new sentence.
